title: Reading and writing a move
outcomes: Names the piece, the squares and any capture, check or castling in a written move
Plays an eight-move score on the board, from either colour and on a turned board
Adds a file letter (or a rank number when both pieces share a file) when two pieces of the same kind can make the move
Knows that marks such as ! and ? do not change the move

steps.text: A move record says **which piece** and **where it lands**. K king, Q queen, R rook, B bishop, N knight; a pawn move has no letter. **x** capture, **+** check, **#** checkmate, **O-O** castling kingside (**O-O-O** queenside), **=Q** a pawn becomes a queen. A number counts one White move and Black's reply: 1.e4 d5. Dots (1...d5) mark Black's move when a score starts with it.

steps.caption: A short score, played from the start. Read each record, then watch the move.

line.say: 1.e4: no letter, so a pawn moves, to e4.
1...d5: three dots mark a Black move shown alone. In a row it is written 1.e4 d5.
2.exd5: the e-pawn captures on d5. The x marks a capture.
2...Qxd5: the queen (Q) captures the pawn on d5.
3.Nc3: N is the knight; it lands on c3.
3...Qa5: no x, because nothing is captured on a5.
4.d4: a pawn move again, so there is no letter.

claims.statement: A white pawn stands on e2 at the start.

steps.text: A record must name exactly one move. If two pieces of the same kind can reach the square, add the file the mover leaves from (**Nbd2**); if both stand on the same file, add the rank instead (**R1a3**). The marks **!** and **?** are a writer's opinion; they change nothing. The same record works for either colour and for a board turned around: square names do not change.

steps.title: Is the record enough?
steps.prompt: Two knights, one square, one change. Predict, then check.
Which part of a record made you stop and think: the piece letter, the x, the file letter for two pieces, or the dots for Black? Say what you will check first next time.

sources: standard algebraic notation (FIDE Laws of Chess, Appendix C) [R]
